messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: routing.alert -> high error-rate for /v1/embeddings (region: eu-west-1). Affected customers: 3. severity: P1. trigger: 5xx spike to 30% over 2m. thread: 1801239876

kate (oncall): I'm on it, grabbing context. any recent deploys?

emma (support): customers reporting embeddings returning short chat-like JSON with 'conversation' key and 500s. ticket IDs: #5542, #5543.

ajay (eng-runtime): logs show fallback path is routing embeddings requests to model-variant 'chat-large-v2' instead of 'embed-base-q4'. Looks like an anchor version got stomped during yesterday's routing config push. Sample log:
```
2026-03-14T21:12:43Z routing: req id=abc123 route=embed -> pinned=anchor-20260314 v=2 -> resolved_variant=chat-large-v2 fallback=true
500 GET /v1/embeddings  "runtime: incompatible-variant: expected embed interface"
```

dana (sre): oof. So runtime is trying to call chat endpoint interface for embeddings. Confirmed schema mismatch. That explains 500s.

sam (eng-routing): I see a change in routing policies: anchor 'anchor-20260314' was pushed with a wildcard variant alias that includes chat variants. The intention was to include newer embed quantized variants but alias accidentally matched chat-* names.

kate (oncall): mitigation plan ideas: 1) disable fallback to pinned anchor for embeddings (turn off fallback policy), 2) re-pin route to fallback-safe embed variant, 3) rollback routing alias change. Which is fastest?

ajay (eng-runtime): fastest is to disable fallback on the route level. Command: `redwoodctl routes update --route embeddings-prod --no-fallback` that'll stop redirects to incompatible variants. After that, we can pin a known-good embed variant.

sam (eng-routing): I'm on the alias rollback. Reverting alias will take ~2-3 minutes to propagate. Doing: `routingctl alias revert anchor-20260314 --from=20260314-14`

emma (support): customers are getting timeouts and 500s in their ingestion pipelines. Ticket #5542 says 18% request failure for last 20m for a production job. Need ETA for customer comms.

lewis (product): prioritize comms after we have a mitigation. I'll draft a short customer note: acknowledge degradation, ETA 30m, post-mortem promised.

kate (oncall): executing mitigation step 1 now. `redwoodctl routes update --route embeddings-prod --no-fallback`

incident-bot: action accepted: routes.update called by kate. job id=job-7743.

kate (oncall): job succeeded. Confirming: new requests are now returning 429 or routing error instead of being redirected. We should pin to embed variant next.

ajay (eng-runtime): pinning to known-good variant: `redwoodctl pin set --route embeddings-prod --variant embed-base-q4v3` will force explicit variant. Doing it now.

incident-bot: pin.set completed by ajay. pin id=pin-9981.

sam (eng-routing): alias revert completed. The alias mapping no longer matches chat-* patterns.

kate (oncall): running synthetic check against /v1/embeddings with sample payload.

kate (oncall): good news — responses look correct now and 200s returned. Verified embed vectors length 1536.

emma (support): updating tickets: "Mitigation applied, embeddings route pinned to embed-base-q4v3 and fallback disabled. We're monitoring for 30 minutes before full reopen." Customers asked for root cause; we'll coordinate postmortem.

dana (sre): temporarily raising throttling to avoid catching cold starts from pinned variant. `infractl throttle set embeddings-prod 0.8` (80% of usual QPS) until steady.

ajay (eng-runtime): adding guard in runtime to reject incompatible variant interfaces instead of trying to call them — will push a small patch but not part of mitigation.

sam (eng-routing): root cause summary for postmortem: a routing alias change added a pattern that inadvertently included chat variants. Alias language allowed wildcard 'chat-*' and 'embed-*' but we used a broad expression. Also lacked a lint rule to detect type-incompatible variants in an alias.

lewis (product): customer impact: 3 customers experienced increased 5xx rates for embeddings ingestion. One customer (enterprise) had background batch jobs delayed ~2 hours; support notified. Financial impact TBD.

kate (oncall): current status: errors back down to baseline, no new pages in last 4m. Keeping incident open for monitoring.

incident-bot: Pager cleared (alert=1801239876).

emma (support): rough timeline for comms: initial short update now, in-product banner for affected customers in 1h, and detailed postmortem in 48h.

ajay (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) add alias lint check to CI (block wildcard patterns that overlap incompatible variant types), 2) add a runtime guard to detect interface mismatch and fail fast, 3) add automated smoke tests for each route that validate variant contract after routing changes.

sam (eng-routing): I'll file the PR for alias lint today and include testcases for chat vs embed mismatches.

dana (sre): monitored for 15 more minutes, looks stable. We'll drop throttling after traffic normals.

kate (oncall): closing notes: incident handled, mitigation applied (no-fallback + pin). Postmortem owners: sam (routing) and ajay (runtime). Support lead: emma. Product comms: lewis.

lewis (product): thanks team. I'll own the customer comms, ping when draft ready. :thumbsup:

emma (support): drafting initial message now.

kate (oncall): filing incident ticket and marking as monitoring -> resolved in 45m unless further regressions.

sam (eng-routing): PR #4521 drafted for alias lint.

ajay (eng-runtime): small runtime PR queued for fast-fail on interface mismatch.

incident-bot: Thread archived after 30 days of inactivity."
